LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION MARKS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, part of Strand 2 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to punctuate a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of punctuating sentences accurately.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. recognise the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in texts,

   Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in sentences,

   Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the importance of punctuating sentences accurately.

   Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read print or non-print texts and identify the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark,

2. punctuate a text using the target punctuation marks,

3. write a short story or dialogue on the theme of science and health education using the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read print or non-print texts and identify the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark,
2. punctuate a text using the target punctuation marks,
3. write a short story or dialogue on the theme of science and health education using the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: It is developed as learners use digital devices as they play online games and record dialogues.

• Self-efficacy is achieved as learners pay attention to detail while role-playing and recording dialogues.

Values:
Unity is achieved as learners give each other feedback on charts and posters featuring the use of punctuation marks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Effective communication is exhibited through well-punctuated texts.

• Social skills are enhanced as learners discuss the effectiveness of punctuation marks in expressing meaning.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of proper punctuation in other learning areas such as Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. recognise the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in texts,
2. use the full stop, exclamation mark, and question mark in sentences,
3. acknowledge the importance of punctuating sentences accurately.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to punctuate a text?
